messages:
evelyn: Heads-up — nightly perf regression spike on mixtral-7b under our Triton+Flash path, p99 up ~15% compared to last week. Repro on ded infra and hosted. :thinking:
perf-bot: nightly-run: regression detected for mixtral-7b @ 2026-03-17T04:12Z (p99 +15%, median +2%). Dashboard: https://ci.redwood/ perf/12345
ravi: can you paste the exact config you used? kernel, batch sizes, seq len distribution?
evelyn: repro command: `./run_bench --model mixtral-7b --kernel flash --batch 4 --seq-dist "[8:0.6,64:0.3,512:0.1]" --rope-scale 1.0 --head-dim 96`

evelyn: quick profiler excerpt (top CPU/GPU ops):
```
GPU kernel times (ms):
flash_attn_forward  0.84  (was 0.65)
matmul_kv_write     0.21  (was 0.07)
kv_reorder_cpy      0.34  (new)
triton_sdp_forward  1.05  (fallback path)
```

akshay: interesting — head_dim is 96 so %16==0, but logs show fallback to sdp. we need the runtime log line (kernel-selector) showing why it fell back.
evelyn: got it, paste from runtime: `[kernel-selector] chosen=flash reason=ok; fallback: sdpa reason=head_dim_align_mismatch (head_dim%8!=0 after rounding)`
denise: wait head_dim%8!=0? we passed 96. maybe padding logic is applying per-attention-head split after kv interleaving. Could be kv layout + RoPE scaling code causing a miscalc.
ravi: also noticed `kv_reorder_cpy` in profiler — that's a new memcpy introduced in the Flash->SDPA compatibility shim. That will kill p99 when sequences are short and we can't amortize the copy.
evelyn: I dug more: Mixtral model variant uses nonstandard kv_dim packing: num_heads=32, head_dim=75 on some sharded checkpoints we onboarded last month. The nightly run pulled that variant for a subset of requests.`

ekshay: (typo fixed) akshay: ahhh that explains it — head_dim 75 is not a multiple of 8/16 so FlashAttn rejects it; runtime currently falls back to SDPA but we do a conservative reorder that copies KV into a padded buffer (kv_reorder_cpy). That extra copy + SDPA kernel matmul overhead explains p99 jump.
denise: plus RoPE scaling path (we recently added dynamic rope scaling) adds another memcpy when scale!=1.0 because we precompute scaled cos/sin and reencode keys in a temp buffer. For mixed head_dim shapes that's O(N*H*hd) work.
evelyn: TL;DR: three factors: (1) odd head dim variants (75) cause fallback, (2) fallback adds KV reorder copies, (3) dynamic RoPE scaling triggers extra transforms — combined they increase p99 for small seqs.

ravi: proposals?
akshay: options: 1) implement padded-Flash path: allocate padded KV buffers (pad head_dim up to next multiple of 8) and run Flash with masked pads. Avoid expensive reorder by emitting KV in padded layout from the encoder. 2) improve kernel-selector heuristics: prefer SDPA only when seqs are long AND head_dim obviously incompatible; for short seqs prefer padded-flash to save latency. 3) avoid double-copy: change RoPE scaling pipeline to operate in-place on KV buffer or fuse with kv layout transform so we only touch memory once.
denise: +1 for fusing RoPE scaling with kv layout transform. That requires careful CUDA kernel but reduces mem-bound overhead.
evelyn: how risky is padded-Flash? Any correctness issues with masking or attention positions?
akshay: implementation details: we need to ensure masked positions don't read the padded slots (we already support padding in Flash kernels via mask tensor). We'll need to pass an updated mask and provide stride/leading-dim adjustments. Edge-case: Triton FlashAttn relies on head_dim multiple-of-8 for vectorized loads; padding to next multiple is straightforward. The main risk is increased memory footprint and a tiny compute overhead on padded slots. For head_dim=75, pad->80 so +6/75 ~8% extra compute on attn kernel — still better than memcpy+SDPA for short seqs.
ravi: we should add a microbenchmark that compares three strategies for head_dim%8!=0: fall back SDPA, padded-Flash, and per-request model rewrite (force quantized head layout). Include varying seq lengths and batch sizes.

evelyn: I can add that microbench to perf harness. Suggested naming: `bench/mixtral_headpad_vs_sdpa.py`. I'll run for seq=[8,64,256], batch=[1,4,8], head_dim=[75,96] and rope_scale=[1.0,1.12].
denise: also add metric probes to runtime: `kernel_selector.choice_reason`, `kv_reorder_bytes`, `rope_inplace_misses` so we can correlate regressions automatically.
akshay: note: Triton fallback sometimes triggers because of masking bug when attention mask is non-contiguous (we pass nested padded batched-sizes). We should add an assert in Flash wrapper that flattens mask to contiguous bool array; that would reduce spurious fallbacks.
evelyn: logged an issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/987 with the repro and profiler attachments.

perf-bot: perf-dashboard: new microbench job created by evelyn (#mixtral-pad-test). Results ETA 2h.

ravi: action items: evelyn - add microbench + link; akshay - prototype padded-flash + mask-flatten; denise - explore fused rope+layout kernel; i'll own the selection heuristic change + metrics.
evelyn: will kick off microbench now. Initial run shows padded-flash median ~5% slower than ideal flash but p99 improved by ~20% vs SDPA fallback for batch=1 seq=8. Posting full numbers when done. :thumbsup:
akshay: if early numbers look good we can gate padded-flash behind a new runtime flag `--enable-headpad` and roll out canary to 10% traffic on Dedicated.
ravi: excellent. please update the incident board if p99 persists in next nightly.
evelyn: will do. Thanks all.
